sources.entry: C#: _C# Networking: Create a TCP chater server, TCP games, UDP Pong and more_

summary.title: Preface
summary.one_liner: This series teaches how to use C#'s System.Net networking API from the command line, with full source code for each tutorial section.
takeaways: The series focuses on C#'s System.Net API rather than general networking theory.
Examples are console-only, targeting Mono on Linux, and should also work with Microsoft's .NET runtime.
Each tutorial section includes full source code, released under the Unlicense (public domain) unless noted otherwise.
Testing across a remote machine or cloud VM is recommended to see real-world network behavior.
On Ubuntu, install Mono from the official project repository and the ca-certificates-mono package for SSL support.
summary.summary: The preface introduces a tutorial series on using C#'s System.Net networking classes, written because the author found existing C# networking material poorly organized. It sets scope: command-line examples only, Mono as the primary runtime with .NET compatibility expected, and minimal extra dependencies. It also explains how to use the guide (follow the numbered sequence, type code rather than copy it, test between machines) and where source code lives. The listing names topics such as a TCP chat server, TCP games, and UDP Pong, but this page itself is only the introduction.
